title: Anxiety and Trust in God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Anxiety and trust in God teaches that believers are called to bring fear, worry, and care to the Lord through prayer, truth, and dependence on His Fatherly care. Trust does not deny anxiety; it brings anxiety under God’s promises.
summary: Anxiety and trust in God teaches that believers are called to bring fear, worry, and care to the Lord through prayer, truth, and dependence on His Fatherly care. Trust does not deny anxiety; it brings anxiety under God’s promises.
christFocus: Jesus Christ teaches His people to trust the Father who knows their needs. Through Him, believers come to God with their fears and receive peace, help, and care.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Anxiety is a real burden in a fallen world. Scripture does not mock fearful people, but it does call them to bring their cares to God rather than being ruled by them.

Jesus teaches that the Father knows what His people need. The birds and lilies become reminders that God cares for His creation and much more for His children.

Prayer is a God-given response to anxiety. Believers are invited to present requests to God with thanksgiving, casting cares on Him because He cares for them.

Trust grows as the heart returns to God’s character, promises, and presence. Peace is not found in controlling every outcome, but in knowing the Lord who holds His people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many anxious believers feel ashamed for being afraid. Others try to control everything because trust feels unsafe. This doctrine gives a faithful path: bring fear to God and learn to rest under His care.

It also guards against simplistic answers. Anxiety may require practical help, wise counsel, and patient support, but the believer’s deepest refuge remains the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When anxiety rises, turn your cares into prayer. Name your fears before God, remember His care, take wise steps where needed, and refuse to let worry become your master. Walk with others who can help you stay anchored in truth.
